gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend: Lexend reads big and open, with oversized lowercase and curves that keep their thickness all the way round. But Bevellier carries the stencil-cut grace, tight and flat, while the sans stays approachable.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-deca: Stencil-cut grace on top, an unshaded line below. Bevellier's tight, high lowercase sets the mood, while Lexend Deca's plain sans line never swells, and that shared flatness is what ties them.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-exa: Bevellier cuts its single-weight strokes flat, like stencil work, with tightly fitted letters and a high, wide lowercase. Lexend Exa shares that flatness, a plain sans whose thickness never shifts.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga tracks its flat, single-weight letters wide, giving every word room to breathe. Yet Bevellier is the showpiece for graceful, stencil-cut display, while the sans-serif handles steady text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-mega: Stencil-cut grace in the heading, then a body that looks drawn with a single nib. Bevellier packs its letters close, while Lexend Mega's plain sans leaves a visible gap in every c and stands nearly capital-height.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-peta: Flat, stencil-cut strokes of a single weight give Bevellier its graceful, high-lowercase look. Lexend Peta sits against it with unthinned curves and a wide-mouthed c, loose beside the tight display.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws a single plotter-pen line, with every round letter open-faced. Lexend Tera's wide stepping-stone sans spacing against Bevellier's graceful, tight-fitted, stencil-cut display is the pair's whole story.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-lexend-zetta: Graceful and tightly fitted, Bevellier cuts flat stencil-like strokes up top. Lexend Zetta's widely tracked plain sans, with constant-width strokes and tall small letters, would make a paragraph feel spread out and easy-going.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-liter: Stencil-cut grace over a body with no stroke contrast at all. Bevellier does the graceful, tight-fitted display work, while Liter's sans, with towering lowercase and wide-mouthed rounds, handles the text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-mada: Mada is a plain sans with curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, against Bevellier's monoline, stencil-cut display. Bevellier stays monoline and tight throughout; Mada opens up.
